correctness.rationale: A unitary two-coordinate cyclic Fourier transform decomposes left convolution on the dihedral regular representation into p explicit 2-by-2 blocks (with opposite, not conjugated, frequencies for complex coefficients). Single-coset supports reduce to a three-term prime Fourier polynomial with 0,1,2 attainable zero frequencies, via Chebotarev nonzero minors and explicit coefficients. Mixed supports normalize to \(e,r,s\) with nonzero a,b,c; the determinant \(a^2+b^2-c^2+ab(z+z^{-1})\) makes the \(j=0\) singularity disjoint from at most one \(\pm j\) pair of nonzero singular blocks. Every required rank is attained on every fixed support by the displayed coefficients. A direct \(2p\)-by-\(2p\) regular-matrix checker tests all supports at p=3,5,7,11, total 6132 cases; finite numerical ranks are corroborative only.

value.rationale: The exact three-point rank spectrum is a naturally motivated first nontrivial nonabelian sparse Fourier-support classification beyond two points. It gives a complete per-support invariant, all extremal coefficient constructions, a sharp minimum and a structurally forbidden intermediate rank. The cosine pair/trivial character mutual exclusion explains a genuine parity-sensitive spectral gap not obtainable from generic uncertainty bounds. This is not a sampled finite table or an arbitrary parameter slice.
